Entry requirements · 2027 entry

Computer Science BS at Washington University in St. Louis

What Washington University in St. Louis asks of applicants to Computer Science BS for 2027 entry (the 2026–27 application cycle). Each requirement below is labelled verified, partly verified or not verified, with the date it was checked and a link to the official source.

US · All Washington University in St. Louis courses · Computer Science field guide

Entry requirements 2027 entry 7 of 8 verified
SAT / ACT
  • Test-optional; self-reported SAT/ACT scores accepted
  • Applicants from high schools outside the U.S. may choose to submit SAT, ACT, predicted/actual national exam, IB Diploma or A-Level results, three AP scores, or three IB HL scores
Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year U.S. Citizen/Permanent Resident Applicants · WashU: First-Year International Applicants
English language
  • TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test required for international students for whom English is a second language (exemptions case by case)
  • University-wide minimum scores: Duolingo 125, IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 5.0 (new scale)
  • From fall 2027 admission, SAT/ACT scores no longer replace an English test

The minimums are WashU’s university-wide English proficiency minimums (Office for International Students & Scholars), linked from the admissions page; the old-scale TOEFL figure is printed unclearly there (“4.5 ≥ 90”). WashU admissions also publishes scores of its most competitive applicants (TOEFL 100 / 5.0, IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 130), not minimum scores, so those are not shown as requirements.

Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: English Testing Requirements · WashU OISS: English Language Proficiency
Admissions tests

None listed on the official source

Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year U.S. Citizen/Permanent Resident Applicants
Subject prerequisites
  • Not used in Altiora’s matching yet — see the note for the official guidance

Official: WashU does not require specific courses. Successful candidates’ transcripts often include 4 years of English, 4 of mathematics, 3–4 of laboratory science, 3–4 of history/social science and 2+ of one foreign language; engineering (the McKelvey School, where the CS B.S. sits) strongly recommends calculus and recommends chemistry and physics.

Partly verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year U.S. Citizen/Permanent Resident Applicants · WashU McKelvey: Computer Science & Engineering — Undergraduate
A-Level requirements
Grades
Not recorded
Details
International applicants submit examination results including predicted A-Levels; applicants from schools outside the U.S. may submit predicted or actual A-Levels in place of SAT/ACT under WashU’s testing options.
Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year International Applicants · WashU: What We’re Looking For
IB requirements
Overall score
Not recorded
Details
Applicants from schools outside the U.S. may submit predicted or actual IB Diploma results, or three IB HL exam scores if not a Diploma candidate — one must be HL Math for McKelvey Engineering, Olin Business and Arts & Sciences STEM applicants.
Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year International Applicants · WashU: What We’re Looking For
Other qualifications
  • AP exam scores optional and considered if submitted
  • Applicants from schools outside the U.S. may submit three AP exam scores under the testing options — one in math for McKelvey Engineering, Olin Business and Arts & Sciences STEM applicants
Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: What We’re Looking For · WashU: First-Year International Applicants
Other requirements
  • Apply to one undergraduate school (e.g. Engineering, Business)
  • Application includes a 250-word response on what you want to study at college and why, plus the Common/Coalition essay
  • No evaluative interviews; third-party interviews such as InitialView strongly encouraged for international students to show English proficiency (not required)
  • Optional 90-second video
Verified19 Oct 2026WashU: First-Year U.S. Citizen/Permanent Resident Applicants · WashU: First-Year U.S. Citizen/Permanent Resident Applicants · WashU: English Testing Requirements · WashU: Optional Video Supplement
